definition: Delayed feedback is a closed-loop method in which a measured signal is fed back after a time lag to influence ongoing activity. In the source, it refers to using delayed recordings to guide stimulation so as to disrupt overly synchronized oscillations.

reasons: Field mismatch: the provided packet discusses delayed feedback deep brain stimulation to suppress pathological synchronized oscillations in Parkinson’s disease (a neurostimulation/control context), not learning as such.
